questions.q: What protocol does pg_basebackup use to pull data from a running server?
options: The streaming replication protocol
Plain SQL SELECT statements
FTP
A proprietary pg_basebackup-only protocol unrelated to replication
questions.explain: pg_basebackup connects over the same streaming replication protocol a replica uses, but asks for a one-time consistent copy instead of staying connected.

questions.q: What role privilege does pg_basebackup require to connect?
options: The REPLICATION attribute
SUPERUSER only, with no other option
No special privilege is needed
The BACKUP attribute
questions.explain: Because pg_basebackup rides the replication protocol, it needs a role with the REPLICATION attribute plus a permitting pg_hba.conf entry.

questions.q: What does the -X stream flag do during pg_basebackup?
options: Streams the WAL generated during the backup alongside it, keeping the backup self-contained
Streams the backup output directly to a remote FTP server
Disables compression
Forces the backup to run in plain-text SQL format
questions.explain: Streaming WAL alongside the backup ensures the base backup is consistent even if the backup process takes a while to complete.

questions.q: What does restoring a pg_basebackup output by itself actually give you?
options: The database restored to the exact moment the backup finished, nothing more recent
Automatic recovery to any point in time
Only the schema, with no data
A logical SQL dump you can edit
questions.explain: A base backup is a consistent snapshot as of when it completed — recovering to a later moment requires combining it with WAL archiving.

questions.q: What does the -R flag add to a pg_basebackup run?
options: A standby.signal file and primary connection info, making the backup ready to start as a streaming replica
Row-level security policies copied from the primary
A restore_command already configured for point-in-time recovery
Read-only mode on the resulting backup directory
questions.explain: The -R flag writes what's needed to bring the backup up immediately as a standby/replica of the primary it was taken from.
